title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: binds posterity when existing, not before; tip before Hypognosticon
pass_a_gloss: Placeus gladly concedes it would have bound Adam's posterity at the time they existed; that they were bound to keep it at the time they did not yet exist he cannot concede at all. Nature's own law, from which none can be exempted, does not bind to obedience except those who are in existence, and while they are. Those not yet entered into the world are not yet held to observe laws made for those in the world. Israel once received the law in the desert for themselves and posterity—who believes that while they wandered there David or the Virgin Mary already owed to keep that law then? Or that therefore the sins of the first receivers must be imputed to all posterity to the consummation of the ages? Tip before the infant / Hypognosticon deepen.
pass_b_english: I concede freely, however, that it would have bound Adam's posterity at the time they existed; but that at the time they did not exist they were then bound to observe it I can in no way concede. Nature's own law, from which no one can be exempted, does not bind to obedience except those who are in the nature of things, and as long as they are in the nature of things. Those who have not yet entered into the World are not yet held to observe laws laid down for those who are in the World. The Israelites once received the law in the desert for themselves and their posterity; who would believe that at that time, while they were wandering in the same desert, David, or the Virgin Mary, already then owed to observe that law? Or that therefore the sins of those who first received the law were to be imputed to all posterity even to the consummation of the ages?
source_text: Concedo tamen libenter futurum fuisse ut obligaret posteros Adami quo tempore fuissent, at quo tempore non fuissent, eos tunc ad id observandum fuisse obligatos nullo modo concedere possum. Ipsa naturae lex a qua nemo eximi potest, non obligat ad obedientiam, nisi eos, qui sunt in rerum natura, & quamdiu sunt in rerum natura. Qui nondum sunt in Mundum ingressi, nondum tenentur observare leges latas iis qui sunt in Mundo. Acceperant Israelitae olim legem in deserto pro se & posteris; quis credat eo tempore, quo peregrinabantur in eodem deserto, Davidem, aut Mariam Virginem debuisse iam tunc legem illam observare? aut propterea eorum qui primi legem acceperunt, peccata fuisse posteris imputanda omnibus ad saeculorum usque consummationem?
